claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state.
Al or Si can serve as oxygen-resistant alloying additions to HfNbTaTiZr.
A small addition of Al or Si will improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed alloying intervention will cause a protective oxide layer to form.
The resulting oxide layer will be stable and adherent.
A stable, adherent oxide layer will improve oxidation resistance.
The oxidation benefit will occur during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
The relevant oxidation exposure duration is several hours.
The modified alloy will retain its yield strength without significant degradation relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will retain its tensile ductility without significant degradation relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Mechanical performance is to be evaluated in tension at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
A decrease greater than 20% in yield strength or tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy will falsify the hypothesis.
An increase greater than 50% in mass gain or oxide-layer thickness relative to the untreated alloy will falsify the hypothesis.
The optimal identity and amount of the alloying addition and its mechanical effects are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires improved oxidation resistance, but the falsification rule permits unchanged oxidation or even up to a 50% increase in mass gain or oxide thickness without falsification. Thus the stated rule does not require the predicted improvement.
